Gold prices find solid support at $4,000 as Standard Chartered sees rally to $4,650 by year-end
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices have managed to hold critical support above $4,000 an ounce even as persistent inflation is pressuring some Federal Reserve officials to take aggressive steps next month. Despite the unrelenting headwinds, one bank remains optimistic that the precious metal will end the year higher. In her latest gold market report published Tuesday, Suki Cooper, Global Head of Commodities Research at Standard Chartered, said that although higher interest rates and a stronger U.S. dollar remain significant obstacles for gold, improving investment flows and robust central bank demand are creating a solid price floor. Despite the difficult environment, Cooper reiterated her forecast for gold prices to average $4,650 an ounce in the fourth quarter, before rising to $4,850 in the first quarter of 2027. Spot gold last traded at $4,031.80 an ounce, unchanged on the day.

Gold, silver rebound after CPI-driven selloff, Hormuz tensions lift crude oil - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were higher in early U.S. trading Wednesday, recovering from Tuesday's sharp losses as bargain hunting and short covering supported precious metals despite elevated Treasury yields and a firmer U.S. dollar. The recovery followed stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data that reinforced expectations for another Federal Reserve rate increase in December, while renewed concerns about shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz provided some underlying support for defensive assets. Spot gold was trading near $4,042.50 an ounce, up $10.70, or 0.27%, while spot silver was trading near $52.690, up $1.270, or 2.47%. Tuesday's U.S. consumer price index increased 0.4% in October, exceeding expectations for a 0.3% gain , while core inflation rose 0.3%, above forecasts for a 0.2% increase. Shelter costs increased 0.3%, food prices advanced 0.5% and energy prices rose 0.7%, indicating continued inflation pressure across several categories. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not publish annual October inflation rates because comparable observations were unavailable following the October 2025 government shutdown. The inflation surprise followed Friday's stronger-than-expected employment report, which showed 165,000 new jobs in October, unemployment falling to 4.1% and average hourly earnings increasing 0.4%. Together, the reports strengthened expectations that the Fed will maintain a restrictive monetary policy stance. Market positioning remains focused on the possibility of a larger Federal Reserve rate increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting. Following Tuesday's inflation report, interest rate futures priced in approximately an 88% probability of a 25-basis-point increase and a 12% probability of a 50-basis-point move , leaving an increase effectively fully priced. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller indicated that persistent core inflation could justify a larger adjustment. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly exceeded 5.00% Tuesday before easing toward 4.98%, while the dollar index remained firm near 102.30. Higher yields and expectations for additional tightening continue to limit gold's recovery. The next important U.S. releases are Thursday's weekly jobless claims and Friday's October producer price index, both scheduled for 8:30 a.m. EST. Softer producer inflation could provide some relief to bullion, while another upside surprise would reinforce December tightening expectations. U.S. Treasury markets are closed Wednesday for Veterans Day, although equity trading continues.
